# Classroom

> Cybersecurity blog by Animesh Roy -- CTF walkthroughs, malware analysis, penetration testing, and security research.

CTF walkthroughs, malware analysis, penetration testing, and security research by Animesh Roy.

## Posts

- [TryHackMe Volt Typhoon: Retracing an APT Through Three Log Sources](https://classroom.anir0y.in/post/thm-room-volttyphoon/): Walkthrough of TryHackMe Volt Typhoon: reconstructing a full living-off-the-land intrusion in Splunk from ADSelfService Plus, wmic and PowerShell logs — the password reset at 11:10:22, the voltyp-admin account, an ntdsutil AD database dump renamed to cl64.gif, a certutil-decoded ASPX web shell and four event logs cleared.
- [TryHackMe Advanced Packet Analysis: What the Logs Could Not Tell You](https://classroom.anir0y.in/post/thm-room-advancedpacketanalysis/): Walkthrough of TryHackMe Advanced Packet Analysis: triaging a SYN scan with TShark, decoding base64 C2 tasking, pulling cleartext FTP credentials, exporting and hashing malware from a PCAP, and reading JA4 fingerprints.
- [TryHackMe Network Monitoring with Zeek: One uid, Five Logs, One Intrusion](https://classroom.anir0y.in/post/thm-room-networkmonitoringwithzeek/): Walkthrough of TryHackMe Network Monitoring with Zeek: reading conn.log, dns.log, http.log, ssl.log and files.log with zeek-cut to find a Cobalt Strike beacon, DNS tunnel and 5 MB exfil POST, then tuning a Notice script from 23 alerts down to 10.
- [TryHackMe Post-Incident Activity: Turning an Incident Into Detection Rules](https://classroom.anir0y.in/post/thm-room-postincidentactivity/): Walkthrough of TryHackMe Post-Incident Activity: reconstructing the full Nexus Financial attack timeline across three M365 sourcetypes in Splunk, calculating dwell time, and converting the IOC tracker into correlated detection rules.
- [TryHackMe Detection and Analysis: Scoping a Nexus Financial Account Compromise](https://classroom.anir0y.in/post/thm-room-detectionandanalysis/): Walkthrough of TryHackMe Detection and Analysis: validating an L1 escalation in Splunk, tracing an M365 account compromise from phishing email to inbox rule, and scoping a second victim the alert never mentioned.
- [TryHackMe DetectMare: Five Broken Detections and a Red Team That Attacks Your Filters](https://classroom.anir0y.in/post/thm-room-detectmare/): Walkthrough of TryHackMe DetectMare: tuning five Sigma detections through a Detection-as-Code pipeline whose red-team check actively bypasses your exclusions, across an APT21 chain from a .docm lure to LSASS dumping, pass-the-hash and a password-protected rar.
- [TryHackMe Sigma Language: Write Once, Convert Everywhere, Tune the Rest](https://classroom.anir0y.in/post/thm-room-sigmalanguage/): Walkthrough of TryHackMe Sigma Language: rule anatomy on a real SigmaHQ rule, writing a recon detection from scratch, converting it to SPL, KQL and EQL with sigma-cli, and fixing six syntax bugs across three broken rules.
- [TryHackMe AI & Automation in Detection Engineering Walkthrough](https://classroom.anir0y.in/post/thm-room-aiautomationdetectioneng/): Walkthrough of TryHackMe AI & Automation in Detection Engineering: a full Detection-as-Code pull request review in TryGitMe, the three bugs that kept a print.exe rule at TP 0/6, and an AI copilot that writes a flawless DCSync rule for someone else's environment.
- [TryHackMe Intro to Detection Engineering Walkthrough](https://classroom.anir0y.in/post/thm-room-introtodetectioneng/): Walkthrough of TryHackMe Intro to Detection Engineering: the DE life cycle, precision vs recall, detection library decay, and all eight flags from the Senna assessment.
- [TryHackMe Monitoring AWS Workloads Walkthrough](https://classroom.anir0y.in/post/thm-room-monitoringawsworkloads/): Walkthrough of TryHackMe Monitoring AWS Workloads: Falco syscall telemetry on EC2 and inside containers, a command injection to reverse shell, and a Lambda function repurposed into a cryptomining launcher via SSM.
- [TryHackMe Monitoring AWS Services Walkthrough](https://classroom.anir0y.in/post/thm-room-monitoringawsservices/): Walkthrough of TryHackMe Monitoring AWS Services: a public S3 bucket policy and the filename brute force that followed, SSH open to the world on EC2, an Internet-exposed RDS instance that needed two changes, IAM discovery, and Denial of Wallet.
- [TryHackMe Monitoring AWS Logins Walkthrough](https://classroom.anir0y.in/post/thm-room-monitoringawslogins/): Walkthrough of TryHackMe Monitoring AWS Logins: console logins and MFAUsed, AKIA vs ASIA access keys, an S3 data-extortion attack, AssumeRole session names, and a Splunk integration authenticating as root.
- [TryHackMe Investigating with Splunk Walkthrough](https://classroom.anir0y.in/post/thm-room-investigatingwithsplunk/): Walkthrough of TryHackMe Investigating with Splunk: a homoglyph backdoor account, WMIC lateral movement, Sysmon registry artefacts, and decoding an Empire PowerShell stager to recover its C2 URL.
- [TryHackMe AWS Security Logging Walkthrough](https://classroom.anir0y.in/post/thm-room-awssecuritylogging/): Walkthrough of TryHackMe AWS Security Logging: CloudTrail console logins and bucket creation, three GuardDuty findings ending in an XMRig miner, CloudFront access logs, and the S3 data event that ties the intrusion together.
- [TryHackMe Cloud Security Pitfalls Walkthrough](https://classroom.anir0y.in/post/thm-room-cloudsecuritypitfalls/): Walkthrough of TryHackMe Cloud Security Pitfalls: IaaS/PaaS/SaaS, the Shared Responsibility Model, why cloud logging is the real obstacle to SIEM coverage, and both challenge flags.
- [TryHackMe Microsoft Intune Monitoring Walkthrough](https://classroom.anir0y.in/post/thm-room-msintunemonitoring/): Walkthrough of TryHackMe Microsoft Intune Monitoring: tracing a remote device wipe through the Intune audit log, PowerShell scripts running as SYSTEM via the Management Extension, and why one laptop has three different GUIDs.
